issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's convention, Jordan chains v^{(i,j,1)},...,v^{(i,j,m_{ij})} start at the eigenvector v^{(i,j,1)}, so the mini-blocks have 1's on the superdiagonal and V^{-1}A=JV^{-1} gives w^{(i,j,k)}A = lambda_i w^{(i,j,k)} + w^{(i,j,k+1)} for k<m_{ij}. Hence only the LAST row of each block is a left eigenvector: w^{(i,j,m_{ij})}A = lambda_i w^{(i,j,m_{ij})}. The claim that the rows w^{(i,j,1)} are left eigenvectors is therefore false whenever some chain has length m_{ij}>1, i.e. in the defective case the paper explicitly treats. The paper's own non-diagonalizable example confirms this: with the displayed V^{-1} and A (label matrixJordan), r_1=0, the first row w^{(1,1,1)}=(1,1,0) satisfies w^{(1,1,1)}A=(1,1,1)=w^{(1,1,2)}, not r_1 w^{(1,1,1)}=(0,0,0), whereas w^{(1,1,2)}=(1,1,1) satisfies w^{(1,1,2)}A=(0,0,0)=r_1 w^{(1,1,2)}; consistently, the paper uses w^{(1,1,2)} (not w^{(1,1,1)}) in the left-eigenvector role in K_infty(y_0)=1/|w-hat^{(1,1,2)} y-hat_0|.

failure_location.quote: The columns $v^{(i,j,1)}$ and the rows $w^{(i,j,1)}$ are \emph{(right) eigenvectors} and \emph{left eigenvectors}, respectively, corresponding to $\lambda_i$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the clause to state that the left eigenvectors are the last rows w^{(i,j,m_{ij})} of the Jordan blocks (equivalently, w^{(i,j,k)}A = lambda_i w^{(i,j,k)} + w^{(i,j,k+1)} for k<m_{ij}); no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The false statement is confined to the Jordan-basis notation bullet. All downstream material already uses the correct rows: Q_1(t) pairs v^{(i,j,1)} with w^{(i,j,M_1)} (right eigenvector times left eigenvector), the RLGE condition uses alpha_{ijM_1}, Section 7.7 uses w^{(1,1,2)}, and Sections 4-6 restrict to simple eigenvalues (m_{ij}=1), where first and last rows coincide. No theorem, formula, or example is invalidated, but as written the bullet asserts a false structural fact about the left generalized eigenvectors in the general (defective) case.
issues.title: Left eigenvectors misidentified as the first rows w^{(i,j,1)} of V^{-1}
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single local clause correction in the notation section. Every substantive claim, formula, and example already conforms to the correct identification (Q_1(t), RLGE, the Section 7.7 example, and the simple-eigenvalue results where the two indices coincide), so all results, rates, and guarantees survive unchanged and no dependent result is affected.
